summary: The report examines how the U.S. is defending critical national infrastructure (energy, water, transportation, finance) against growing cyber threats, centered on the National Cybersecurity Strategy launched September 15, 2023. It stresses education, workforce training, public-private partnerships, AI-enhanced technology, resilience, public awareness, and international alliances. Experts quoted argue that cybersecurity is now a national security and public safety matter requiring proactive, collaborative effort.
one_line: The U.S. National Cybersecurity Strategy and related education, workforce, private-sector, resilience, and international efforts aim to protect critical infrastructure from escalating cyber threats.
key_facts: The government launched the National Cybersecurity Strategy on September 15, 2023, focusing on strengthening defenses, promoting resilience, and setting protocols for responding to and recovering from cyber incidents.
On November 12, 2023, a coordinated cyber attack momentarily disrupted power distribution in three U.S. states, causing widespread confusion and near-panic.
Critical national infrastructure sectors named include energy, water treatment, transportation, and finance.
The Federal Cyber Corps program, introduced just after the National Cybersecurity Strategy, offers scholarships in exchange for post-graduation government service; director Mark Walters leads it.
The Federal Cyber Corps targeted an initial enrollment of 3,000 students across various universities by the end of 2023.
Dr. Alexis Thompson of the National Cyber Security Alliance says the strategy aims to integrate cybersecurity learning into every stage of education, from primary schools to higher education.
A joint public-private summit was held on December 1, 2023, where Carolyn Hughes, CISO at GridTech Solutions, said no single entity can tackle the cybersecurity challenge alone.
The Cyber Innovation Challenge, launched in late 2023, encourages startups and academics to develop tools for threat intelligence and mitigation; Gregory Benton is a jury member.

The Critical Infrastructure Resilience Institute held a workshop on September 20, 2023, where energy, water, and finance participants tested attack scenarios; coordinator Jay Hernandez said resilience is about adapting and evolving.
CyberSmart Week ran from November 9 to 16, 2023, to educate the public on simple cybersecurity practices.
At the Global Cybersecurity Summit on October 25, 2023, the U.S. and allies unveiled the Cyber Collaboration Framework pact for coordinating responses to international cyber threats.
Janet Kline, U.S. envoy for Cyber Affairs, said cybersecurity challenges are global and so must be the efforts to address them.
